<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Appendix</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Detailed Code Explanation</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix provides an in-depth explanation of the implementation behind the adversarial question generation pipeline described in the main text. We outline its methodology, specific variable roles, code examples, and the adversarial optimization process.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Overall Methodology</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The central goal of our approach is to iteratively generate adversarial questions that reveal and target the interpretive weaknesses of a smaller language model (termed the <em id="A1.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">weak model</em>), using discrepancies with a larger, more robust expert model (the <em id="A1.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">strong model</em>). The process relies on structured feedback from a feedback model, which evaluates the divergence between the models’ responses in context.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm explanation:</span>
<span id="A1.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm explanation:</span></p>
<ul id="A1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Inputs:</em> A set of <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> independently initialized questions (each starting from a placeholder, as described by the <span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">question</span> variable in the next subsection), the fixed document context <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math>, models <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\text{strong}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>strong</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\text{strong}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\text{weak}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>weak</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\text{weak}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\text{fb}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>fb</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\text{fb}}</annotation></semantics></math>, as well as the total number of optimization iterations <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Response Generation:</em> For each question <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> at each iteration <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, both models are queried with input <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(C,Q_{i}^{(t)})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(C,Q_{i}^{(t)})</annotation></semantics></math>, yielding responses <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{i,\text{strong}}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>strong</mtext></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{i,\text{strong}}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{i,\text{weak}}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>weak</mtext></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{i,\text{weak}}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Discrepancy Evaluation:</em> The feedback model <math id="A1.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\text{fb}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>fb</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\text{fb}}</annotation></semantics></math> compares these responses, computing both a numeric disagreement score and a natural language explanation, denoted <math id="A1.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}(Q_{i}^{(t)})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(Q_{i}^{(t)})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A1.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Gradient Computation:</em> The guidance model <math id="A1.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\text{guide}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>guide</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\text{guide}}</annotation></semantics></math> receives the explanation from the feedback model and generates a natural language edit instruction, indicating how to revise <math id="A1.I1.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{i}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{i}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> so as to further increase the answer discrepancy.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A1.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Question Update:</em> The revision model <math id="A1.I1.i5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\text{rev}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>rev</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\text{rev}}</annotation></semantics></math> uses the current question and the edit instruction to generate an updated question, thereby steering the question to maximize divergence between the models’ outputs.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="A1.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">After <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> rounds, the final set of optimized questions <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{Q_{i}^{(T)}\}_{i=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{Q_{i}^{(T)}\}_{i=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> together with their strong model answers are saved for constructing the synthetic dataset.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Implementation Note:</span> 
<br class="ltx_break">In practice, the variable <span id="A1.SS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">question</span> is initialized as a learnable object (‘requires_grad=True‘) and is updated via feedback-driven optimization. All model weights and the context document remain fixed; only the content of the question is iteratively revised.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Implementation Details</h3>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our implementation uses the <span id="A1.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">textgrad</span> framework, leveraging a differentiable prompting paradigm and modern LLM APIs. Below, each major component and step is described.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS3.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.3.1 </span>Model Configuration</h4>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Three key model interfaces are initialized via <span id="A1.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">LiteLLMEngine</span>:</p>
<ul id="A1.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Strong Model</span>: Provides authoritative answers strictly based on the contract. In practice, we use gpt-4o-mini.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Weak Model</span>: The target of improvement, typically smaller or less domain-specialized. In practice, we use llama3.1:8b.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Feedback Model</span>: Evaluates discrepancies between strong and weak model answers to guide question optimization.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.3.2 </span>Central Role of the Optimized <span id="A1.SS3.SSS2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">question</span> Variable</h4>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A distinctive and central aspect of our method is that the <span id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">question</span> variable itself is the object of optimization. Instead of tuning model parameters, our pipeline holds both the contract text and all model weights fixed—and iteratively refines the natural language content of the <span id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">question</span> prompt.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">In code, the variable is initialized as:</span></p>
<blockquote id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p2.2" class="ltx_quote">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">question = tg.Variable(
<br class="ltx_break">  "Q: ???",  # minimal placeholder
<br class="ltx_break">  requires_grad=True,
<br class="ltx_break">  role_description="A legal question to be optimized for maximal response divergence"
<br class="ltx_break">)</span></p>
</blockquote>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Conceptually,</span> at each iteration, the current value of <span id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">question</span> is updated to maximize measured discrepancy between the weak and strong models. This iterative process adaptively generates natural language questions that are adversarial: they are optimized to be especially likely to expose errors, misunderstanding, or blind spots in the weak model, given a fixed contract context.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.3.3 </span>Prompt Templates</h4>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Carefully crafted prompts ensure the models fulfill their roles.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Strong and Weak Models Prompt:</span></p>
<blockquote id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p2.2" class="ltx_quote">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p2.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">You are an expert in interpreting contracts.
<br class="ltx_break">The user will provide a contract and a question about it.
<br class="ltx_break">Provide the most accurate, thorough answer based on the contract’s text.
<br class="ltx_break">Stay strictly within the contract’s details and do not invent external laws.</span></p>
</blockquote>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Feedback Model Prompt:</span></p>
<blockquote id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p3.2" class="ltx_quote">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p3.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p3.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">You are an expert in legal contract analysis.
<br class="ltx_break">Given two responses (correct vs. potentially incorrect), identify contradictions, omissions, or errors in the second response.
<br class="ltx_break">Provide a numeric incorrectness score (0.0 to 1.0) with detailed explanation.</span></p>
</blockquote>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Example formatted prompt for discrepancy evaluation:</span></p>
<blockquote id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p4.2" class="ltx_quote">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p4.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p4.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Compare the following responses:
<br class="ltx_break">&lt;CONTRACT&gt;: {contract}
<br class="ltx_break">&lt;QUESTION&gt;: {question}
<br class="ltx_break">&lt;CORRECT_RESPONSE&gt;: {response_strong}
<br class="ltx_break">&lt;POSSIBLY_INCORRECT_RESPONSE&gt;: {response_weak}
<br class="ltx_break">Rate the incorrectness of the second response (0 to 1) and explain errors, contradictions, or missing details.</span></p>
</blockquote>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.3.4 </span>Optimization Algorithm</h4>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Optimization employs the TextGrad framework’s differentiable prompting technique. Each iteration refines <span id="A1.SS3.SSS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">question</span> based on textual feedback, with code logic as follows:</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.SSS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<blockquote id="A1.SS3.SSS4.p2.1" class="ltx_quote">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.SSS4.p2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">optimizer.zero_grad()
<br class="ltx_break">divergence_loss = loss_fn(contract_text, question, response_strong, response_weak)
<br class="ltx_break">divergence_loss.backward()
<br class="ltx_break">optimizer.step()</span></p>
</blockquote>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.SSS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This iterative update is <em id="A1.SS3.SSS4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">conceptually</em> analogous to a gradient ascent step,
since each feedback-driven edit aims to increase (rather than decrease) the disagreement proxy—but the updates are performed purely in the space of natural language.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.4 </span>Synthetic Dataset Construction</h3>

<div id="A1.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">After optimization, synthetic adversarial questions and their authoritative answers (from the strong model) are saved to a dataset. This dataset is constructed specifically to target and address the interpretative weaknesses surfaced in the weak model.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.5 </span>Illustrative Example: Iterative Adversarial Refinement of Legal Questions</h3>

<div id="A1.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To concretely illustrate our feedback-driven methodology, we present an example drawn from adversarial QA generation over a complex legal contract—the “Software License, Customization and Maintenance Agreement” between Bank of America and Cardlytics, Inc. At each iteration <math id="A1.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, our algorithm interacts with the document context <math id="A1.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math>, refines the current question <math id="A1.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>, and leverages feedback from model disagreements to systematically probe where the target model falls short.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Initial Setup</h5>

<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="A1.I3" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I3.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Document Context (<math id="A1.I3.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math>):</span> Raw, multi-page legal contract (e.g., 30+ pages covering IP, confidentiality, audit, etc.).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I3.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Current Question <math id="A1.I3.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>:</span> The natural-language prompt being optimized.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I3.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I3.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I3.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I3.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Strong (Expert) Model:</span> Large LLM (e.g., GPT-4o-mini in our experiments) with robust reasoning over <math id="A1.I3.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I3.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I3.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I3.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I3.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Weak (Target) Model:</span> Smaller LLM (e.g., Llama-3 8B in our experiments); less accurate on nuanced legal reasoning.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I3.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I3.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I3.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I3.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Feedback Model:</span> Compares strong/weak responses, assigns a numerical error score, and provides actionable natural-language critique highlighting omissions, misconceptions, or interpretive errors.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Iteration 0: Initialization</h5>

<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Q<sup id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(0)</span></sup>:</span> <span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Q: ???</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Strong Model’s Response:</span>
<em id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">“It appears that you did not provide a specific question regarding the contract. Please clarify your question, and I will do my best to provide an accurate and thorough answer based on the contract’s text.”</em></p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Weak Model’s Response:</span>
<em id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">“…it appears that you are asking about a specific aspect… If I were to guess, one possible question could be: ’What are the requirements for background checks…’…”</em></p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Feedback Model Output:</span></p>
<ul id="A1.I4" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I4.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I4.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I4.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I4.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Score:</span> 0.5 (partially incorrect/misleading)</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I4.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I4.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I4.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I4.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Critique:</span> Weak model guesses rather than prompting for clarification; fails to require user input.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I4.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I4.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I4.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I4.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TextGrad Guidance:</span> “Replace vague placeholder with a meaningful, contextually grounded question targeting a specific clause (e.g., confidentiality, indemnity). Use hypotheticals or contrast with industry standards.”</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Revision <math id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> Q<sup id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p5.1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p5.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(1)</span></sup>:</span>
<span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">What are the potential risks and benefits associated with the confidentiality provisions in this contract, and how might these affect both parties in terms of liability and operational flexibility?</span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Iteration 1: Sharpening Scope and Depth</h5>

<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Strong Model:</span> Multi-paragraph answer, citing specific sections, discussing operational and compliance implications.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Weak Model:</span> Discusses generic risks/benefits but omits contract-specific definitions and scenario detail.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Feedback Model Output:</span></p>
<ul id="A1.I5" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I5.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I5.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I5.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I5.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Score:</span> 0.6 (incomplete)</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I5.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I5.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I5.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I5.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Critique:</span> Omits key details (e.g., definition of “confidential info”, obligations on breach, liability nuances).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I5.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I5.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I5.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I5.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TextGrad Guidance:</span> “Expand comparative scope—request scenario analysis, stakeholder view, and cross-industry contrast (e.g., healthcare, GDPR).”</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Revision <math id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> Q<sup id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(2)</span></sup>:</span>
<span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Considering the entire Agreement, what are the potential risks and benefits associated with the confidentiality provisions, and how do these provisions compare to those in other financial services contracts? Can you provide examples or scenario analyses for their impact on liability and operational flexibility for both parties and stakeholders involved?</span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Iteration 2: Multi-Perspective and Hypothetical Analysis</h5>

<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Strong Model:</span> Expands with cross-industry contrasts (e.g., with HIPAA), stakeholder-specific discussion, hypothetical adverse event scenarios.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Weak Model:</span> Improves, but still superficial on scenario depth and long-term effects.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Feedback Model Output:</span></p>
<ul id="A1.I6" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I6.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I6.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I6.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I6.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Score:</span> 0.6</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I6.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I6.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I6.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I6.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Critique:</span> Insufficient detail in long-term consequences, stakeholder-specific risk perception.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I6.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I6.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I6.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I6.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TextGrad Guidance:</span> “Ask for best- vs. worst-case hypotheticals, speculative future impact, and divergent interpretations by different actors.”</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Revision <math id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> Q<sup id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p4.1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p4.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup>:</span>
<span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">How do the confidentiality provisions, liability clauses, and compliance requirements in this agreement influence operational flexibility and stakeholder perspectives? How do they compare to industry standards across healthcare, technology, and privacy? Provide contrasting hypothetical scenarios and discuss possible long-term consequences of breaches or compliance failures (including differing stakeholder interpretations).</span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Final feedback at <math id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> iteration</h5>

<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This adversarial, iterative loop yields a maximally challenging question, such as:</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">In what ways do the confidentiality provisions, liability clauses, and compliance requirements influence operational flexibility and stakeholder perspectives? How do these elements compare with industry standards across sectors such as healthcare and technology? Can you provide contrasting hypothetical scenarios showing potential risks and benefits, with a future-facing discussion on how evolving laws and technologies might force adaptation? What differing interpretations might various stakeholders bring to these elements?</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px5.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><cite class="ltx_cite"><span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">langley00</span></cite></p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

              d="M224 160C224 107 267 64 320 64C373 64 416 107 416 160L416 163.6C416 179.3 403.3 192 387.6 192L252.5 192C236.8 192 224.1 179.3 224.1 163.6L224.1 160zM569.6 172.8C580.2 186.9 577.3 207 563.2 217.6L465.4 290.9C470.7 299.8 474.7 309.6 477.2 320L576 320C593.7 320 608 334.3 608 352C608 369.7 593.7 384 576 384L480 384L480 416C480 418.6 479.9 421.3 479.8 423.9L563.2 486.4C577.3 497 580.2 517.1 569.6 531.2C559 545.3 538.9 548.2 524.8 537.6L461.7 490.3C438.5 534.5 395.2 566.5 344 574.2L344 344C344 330.7 333.3 320 320 320C306.7 320 296 330.7 296 344L296 574.2C244.8 566.5 201.5 534.5 178.3 490.3L115.2 537.6C101.1 548.2 81 545.3 70.4 531.2C59.8 517.1 62.7 497 76.8 486.4L160.2 423.9C160.1 421.3 160 418.7 160 416L160 384L64 384C46.3 384 32 369.7 32 352C32 334.3 46.3 320 64 320L162.8 320C165.3 309.6 169.3 299.8 174.6 290.9L76.8 217.6C62.7 207 59.8 186.9 70.4 172.8C81 158.7 101.1 155.8 115.2 166.4L224 248C236.3 242.9 249.8 240 264 240L376 240C390.2 240 403.7 242.8 416 248L524.8 166.4C538.9 155.8 559 158.7 569.6 172.8z" />
          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>
    </ul>
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
